The wind had finally stopped its restless whispering, and the sea lay flat and silver under the moon. In the tall, white tower at the edge of the cliff, Elias wound the great clockwork mechanism that turned the lighthouse beam. *Click, whir, hum.* The sound was steady and slow, like a heartbeat.

On the railing outside, a single seagull named Pip sat with his wings tucked tight against his chest. He was tired. He had flown all day, chasing the breeze and the scent of fish, but now his legs felt heavy and his eyes were heavy with sleep.

Elias noticed the small gray shape on the railing. He didn’t shoo the bird away. Instead, he opened the heavy iron door just a crack, letting out a sliver of warm, golden light.

"Goodnight, little one," Elias said softly. His voice was low, barely louder than the rustle of his wool coat.

Pip tilted his head. He didn’t fly away. He simply blinked, once, and then closed his eyes.
